decision.label: ANSWER
decision.response:
For your 0.24 ha garlic plot in southern Tigray, using the extension worker's rates of 200 kg/ha NPS and 150 kg/ha urea:

- NPS: 200 kg/ha × 0.24 ha = 48 kg of NPS for the plot. Apply the whole amount at planting (the source states all phosphorus fertilizer is applied once at planting).
- Urea: 150 kg/ha × 0.24 ha = 36 kg of urea for the plot, split into two equal applications: 18 kg at planting and 18 kg 30–45 days after planting.

Note: the source also mentions that in some cases, when there is good rain, urea may be applied in three phases (1/3 at planting, 1/3 after 30 days, and the remaining 1/3 three weeks after the second application). That is an optional alternative; the two-application schedule is the described default.
decision.justification: The southern Tigray common practice rule gives explicit product rates of 200 kg/ha NPS and 150 kg/ha urea for garlic (p.12). Multiplying by the explicit plot area of 0.24 ha yields 48 kg NPS and 36 kg urea. The urea two-split rule states half at planting and the remaining half 30–45 days after planting, giving 18 kg + 18 kg for this plot. The NPS rule notes the whole phosphorus fertilizer is applied once at planting; timing of the entire NPS blend is an inference flagged in the rule, so NPS timing is stated with that qualification. The three-split urea schedule is conditional on 'good rain' (unknown) and is optional, so it is mentioned only as an alternative, not applied.
